weather_report:
Subiaco, at this soft in‑between hour, wears a low whispering sky; light rain is sliding across roofs now and again, with more showers drifting toward dawn. Moonlight is hidden, streetlights haloed in mist, and the night feels rinsed and cool. Sunshine will be scarce until well after first light, and any glimpse of it this morning looks brief; UV is negligible now and gentle at dawn, climbing only if the cloud thins later. The air is fresh and a touch metallic, edges blurred, voices of the street softened.

It’s a gentle, damp start rather than a sparkling one. Dress for drizzle and a hint of chill: a light waterproof, closed shoes, sleeves you can roll if the day brightens, and an umbrella by the door. Roads will be slick, so unhurried is the right speed. This is weather for a calm cup of tea, an early chapter, tidying the week’s loose ends, or a quiet gym visit if the showers ease. If the sun does poke through later, carry sunglasses and a hat; otherwise keep the day close to home, windows cracked to the smell of wet gardens.
